references.text: David declares that he washes his hands in innocence, reflecting the ritual of handwashing as a symbol of purity and freedom from blood guilt.
The psalmist mentions handwashing as a sign of purity, connecting it to the ritual aspect of declaring oneself innocent.
Pilate washes his hands before the crowd to declare himself innocent of Jesus' blood, an action that directly reflects this Old Testament ritual for disclaiming responsibility for blood guilt.
The full context of the ritual concerning an unsolved murder case, where the elders must perform a cleansing ceremony to free the city from blood guilt.
The command that priests should wash their hands and feet before serving, showing the ritual significance of handwashing in Israelite practice.
